To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

opening PICS bags for 30 minutes per week at high grain moisture content (MC) increases the risk of fungal growth and aflatonin contamination, and that the risk is highest when the grain is not properly dried prior to bagging.
repeated exposure of hermetically sealed PICS bags to high moisture conditions will increase fungal growth in the grain and the risk of mycotoxin contamination.
opening PICS bags for consumption increases risk of fungal growth and afltoxin contamination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of opening hermetic bags for maize on fungal growth and mycotoxin contamination.
the impact of opening hermetic bags on fungal growth and mycotoxin accumulation.
understanding the mechanisms that lead to aflatoxin contamination in maize stored in PICS hermetic storage bags.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the opening of the PICS bag for consumption purposes will result in increased fungal growth and aflotoxin accumulation, especially at higher moisture contents.
the PICS bag is not designed to store high moisture content grain for extended periods of time.
opening the bags for a short period (30 min) at high grain moisture (20% MC or higher) will increase fungal growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PICS bags should be used as intended and not opened for routine use.
the PICS bags are effective for insect pest management and fungal growth prevention when properly used, i.e., when grain moisture contents are below 15% and bags are not repeatedly opened.
opening PICS bags for consumption will increase the risk for aflatoxin contamination and should be avoided.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PICS bags should be used to store dry maize (less than 13.5% MC), as recommended by Purdue University and the PICS program.
opening hermetic bags will allow for fungal growth and aflatonin accumulation.
